Mostly unrelated but think of this as a direct message.

In order to beat gaming by users (marketers etc) i recommend the following:

First - do not accumulate user points beyond individual submissions or comments. My article can get voted up and so can my comment but those would not add up into a 'user karma' score of any type. Ask yourself what value this serves? The answer is none!

Second, prevent accounts from voting each other up frequently. This way a group of accounts will not be able to gang up and push articles or comments. The way to implement this is to have a log file that user id Y voted on user id z. Before each comment and article vote is applied have it check against this log first Nd discard it if this user id has already voted on the other user id's post. Dump the log every day or six hours or whatever so effectively users can only vote for each like once a day on an article and a comment.

These two things will knock out the worst sort of users - popularity/reputation seekers, marketers building influence, and interest groups seeking to inhibit natural discussion.

To clarify - my article or comment would accumulate points and show a visible score within the post/discussion but that number would not carry over or be tracked elsewhere - this way each comment stands on its own.
